gap: No result ChatGPT got states that its 'best value' UGREEN Nexode 100W 4-port charger caps the laptop port at 65 W as soon as a second USB-C device is plugged in, which is below the 70 W that Apple says the M5 MacBook Air needs to fast-charge. That leaves two choices: charge the laptop alone at night and refill the 90 Wh power bank in about 1–2 h after it, or plug both in and leave the bank on the 30 W port, which takes at least 3 h (90 Wh ÷ 30 W).
standout_why: Publicasta (cited) and ChatGPT's own answer from the itechguides page it cited both say only that a '100 W' charger 'might give the laptop 65 W when a phone is also plugged in'. They don't give the per-pair table for the UGREEN 100W (itechguides lists the 90928 desktop model and says no two-port split is stated). Neither ties the 65 W to Apple's 70 W fast-charge threshold, and neither works out how long it takes to refill a power bank from the second port. Publicasta has no refill times and no 'charges per bank' figure. Wired couldn't be fetched. So rivals have the 65/30 idea, and the 70 W threshold and the refill-time maths are new.
kit_items: Wall charger: UGREEN Nexode 100W 4-Port (CD226, 3× USB-C + USB-A), bought as the store's bundle with two 100 W USB-C cables. C1 or C2 alone gives up to 100 W, so a MacBook Air fast-charges (needs 70 W or more) only when it is alone on C1. Any second device on C2 holds the laptop to 65 W.

Power bank: UGREEN Nexode Power Bank 25,000 mAh 165W with built-in cables. It is rated 90 Wh, which is under the common 100 Wh carry-on threshold. Its 90 W input means it refills in about 1 h from C1 on its own (90 Wh ÷ 90 W), or in at least 3 h from C2 (30 W) while the laptop sits on C1. Niuxtech measured almost 2 h from a 65 W charger. 90 Wh is 1.67× the 53.8 Wh battery of a 13-inch MacBook Air at nameplate, before conversion losses.
Cables: the two 100 W USB-C cables in the charger bundle. 100 W is at or above anything this charger can put out on one port, and the bank's own 140 W and 65 W cables cover the bank side.
Plug adapter (international only): a plain plug adapter without conversion is enough because the charger accepts 100–240 V (UGREEN FAQ on Manualslib).
